title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/chrome-email-verification/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793091215457.jpg"/><p>Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets the browser confirm email ownership without sending a message. Gmail is the first provider. Developers add form hints and validate a signed token server-side. Commenters question the privacy benefit, and the API is best used as a progressive enhancement.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: an AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-tsrs-ai-typescript/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793039825386.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare, VoidZero and Max Schwenk announced tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with the TypeScript team's involvement. Cloudflare claims up to 8x faster checking and 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, though one test against 7.1 beta showed 2.7x. It lacks watch mode and a language server, and exits with code 2 on type errors.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ngrx-22-angular/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792664456149.jpg"/><p>NgRx 22 adds experimental resource extensions that change Angular's resource behavior, so value() is retained during reloads and no longer throws on errors. It also introduces dynamic deep signals for union types, a SignalStoreFeatureType utility, and ESLint v10 support. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and most breaking changes have automated migrations.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/nestjs-12-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792168374584.jpg"/><p>NestJS version 12 has been released, transitioning core packages to ESM and adding Standard Schema validation. It updates the CLI and introduces an observability SDK. Key changes include project generation choices between CJS and ESM, improved validation options, and lifecycle project hooks. Users will need Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. Migration guides are available for upgrading.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
